source_text: Si quis dicit, perfectum hominem esse Christum divise, et Deum Verbum divise; et non confitetur unum Dominum Iesum Christum, sicut scriptum est; anathema sit. Quomodo dicere quis potest perfectum hominem Christum divise, et Deum Verbum divise; cum ipse Dominus dicat: Quid me quaeritis occidere hominem, qui veritatem loquutus sum, quam audivi a patre? Non enim hominem pro nobis dedit, sed se ipsum pro nobis tradidit Deus Verbum homo propter nos factum. Quapropter dicit: Solvite templum hoc, et in tribus diebus excitabo illud. Ipse autem dicebat de templo corporis sui.
thought_title: Against Dividing Christ into Two Separate Persons
orientation: Gregory condemns the error of saying Christ is a perfect man separately and the Word of God separately, without confessing one Lord Jesus Christ, and supports the unity from Christ's own words and the temple saying.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says [that] a perfect man [is] Christ separately, and [the] Word of God separately; and [does] not confess one Lord Jesus Christ, as it is written; let him be anathema. How [is one] able to say [that] a perfect man [is] Christ separately, and [the] Word of God separately; since [the] Lord himself says: Why [do] you seek to kill a man, who [has] spoken [the] truth, which I heard from [the] father? For not [did] a man give himself for us, but himself he handed over [for] us [the] Word of God [having been] made man on account of us. Wherefore he says: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. He himself however was speaking concerning [the] temple of [his] body.

lemmas.gloss: separately, apart, in a divided manner
to kill, to put to death
he handed over, he delivered up
I will raise up, I will rouse
he was saying, he used to say

choices.why: The adverb modifies how Christ is said to be perfect man and Word of God — divided, apart, not as one unified subject. 'Apart' works but 'separately' is clearer for the logical error.

choices.english: Why do you seek to kill me, a man
choices.why: Christ quotes John 8:40 identifying himself as 'a man who has spoken the truth'; the construction is accusative of the person with an appositional noun.
rejected: Why do you seek to kill a man, me
Why do you seek me to kill a man

choices.term: Non enim hominem pro nobis dedit, sed se ipsum pro nobis tradidit Deus Verbum homo propter nos factum
choices.english: For not a man did he give for us, but the Word of God made man for us handed over himself for us
choices.why: Contrasts giving a mere man with the Word himself giving himself; 'Deus Verbum homo propter nos factum' is the subject of 'tradidit'.
rejected: For he did not give a man for us, but God the Word made man for us gave himself for us
For not a man did he give for us, but the Word of God, made man for us, delivered himself for us

choices.term: Solvite templum hoc, et in tribus diebus excitabo illud
choices.english: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up
choices.why: Standard wording of John 2:19; 'solvite' is plural imperative addressing the Jews.
rejected: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it
Dissolve this temple, and in three days I will raise it up

choices.term: Ipse autem dicebat de templo corporis sui
choices.english: But he was speaking about the temple of his body
choices.why: Narrative explanation from John 2:21; imperfect 'dicebat' shows this was his meaning.
rejected: But he spoke of the temple of his body
But he was saying about the temple of his body

pass_b_english: If anyone says that Christ is a perfect human being separately, and the Word of God separately, and does not confess one Lord Jesus Christ, just as it is written, let him be anathema. How can anyone say that Christ is a perfect human being separately, and the Word of God separately, when the Lord himself says: "Why do you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth that I heard from the Father?" For he did not give a mere human being for us, but the Word of God made human for us handed over himself for us. That is why he says: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up." But he was speaking about the temple of his body (John 8:40; John 2:19-21).
